1.

By way of present judgment/award, I shall dispose of the Dar filed by the investigating agency
which has been converted into a claim petition under section 166(4) of M. V. Act 1988 for grant of
compensation to the petitioners who are Lrs of deceased victim namely Sachin Kumar, aged about
27 years in the road accident on 08.06.2021 at about 5:17 Pm at Bakhtwarpur, Hiranki Road
Opposite, Delhi.
Claimants are parents of the deceased.

2. The concise material facts relevant to decide the present claim are that on 08.06.2021, deceased
namely Sachin Kumar (aged about 27 years) was driving his vehicle bearing no. Dl8C-Ah-3688.

When he reached near Macp No. 406/21; Fir No. 428/21; Ps. Alipur Dod: 16.02.2024 Meadows
Park, suddenly, the driver of offending vehicle bearing no. Dl1Gc-8286 which was being driven by
him at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, came and hit the car of deceased with a
great force, as a result of which, he received fatal injuries and died at the spot.

He was immediately
taken to Kapil Hospital, Main Road, Nathupura, Burari, Delhi where he was medically examined
and declared 'brought dead'.

Postmortem of the deceased was conducted at Bjrm Hospital,
Jahangir Puri, Delhi.

A case U/s 279/304A Ipc was registered at Ps. Alipur vide Fir No. 428/21
with regard to the accident in question.

The petitioners (parents of deceased) have claimed that the
accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of aforementioned offending vehicle
which was allegedly being driven by respondent no.1/driver.

The offending vehicle was found to be
owned by respondent no. 2 and was duly insured with respondent no. 3/Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd.,
at the time of accident in question.

3. The respondent no.1 & 2 i.e. driver and registered owner have failed to file their Ws despite grant
of sufficient time and opportunities.

Subsequently, they have also stopped appearing before this
Tribunal after filing of Dar and accordingly, they were proceeded exparte and their defence was
also struck off vide order dated 19.01.2024.

4 . The insurance company had filed its legal offer, whereby it offered to pay a sum of Rs. 12,67,142/-
after deduction of 50% amount on Macp No. 406/21; Fir No. 428/21; Ps. Alipur Dod: 16.02.2024
account of self negligence on the part of deceased, as compensation towards full and final
satisfaction for the claim raised by petitioners for the fatal injuries suffered by Sachin Kumar in the
accident in question.

However, the said offer was not acceptable to the petitioners in the present

10. During the arguments, Ld. Counsel for petitioners heavily relied upon criminal case record (which is part of DAR Ex. PW1/3 colly) in support of case of petitioners in order to bring home that the accident in question had taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle i.e. Canter bearing Registration No. DL1GC-8286, by its driver/respondent no. 1.

It has been contended that respondent no. 1 Sh. Saddam was also chargesheeted by police for offences punishable U/s 279/304A IPC, which clearly establishes that the accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no. 1.

Per contra, it is contended MACP No. 406/21; FIR No. 428/21; PS. Alipur DOD: 16.02.2024 on behalf of insurance company that PW1 Sh. Naresh Kumar is not an eyewitness of the accident, as such his testimony should not be considered on this issue.
It is further counter argued that the accident in question was occurred due to sole negligence of the deceased as he was driving his car at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner.

11. During the arguments, Ld. Counsel for the petitioners heavily relied upon the criminal case record (which is part of DAR Ex. PW1/6 colly) in support of their case in order to bring home that the accident in question had taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no. 1.

It has been contended that respondent no. 1 Sh. Saddam was also charge-sheeted by police for offences punishable U/s 279/304A IPC, which clearly establishes that the accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no. 1.
12.

It is pertinent to note that the respondent no.1/driver of offending vehicle was the other material witness to throw light by testifying as to how and under what circumstances, the accident has taken place.
However, he has preferred not to enter into the witness box.

Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle i.e. Canter bearing registration no. DL1GC-8286 by the respondent no.1.
There is nothing on record to show that the petitioners had any enmity with the driver of the offending vehicle so as to falsely implicate him in this case.

Further, the postmortem report (which is part of DAR)
also corroborates that cause of death of deceased was hemorrhagic shock as a result of abdominal injuries due to blunt force impact.
All the injuries were antemortem in nature and possible in manner as alleged.
The injuries as mentioned in the relevant column of external injuries of the said report, are also consistent with the injuries which are sustained in road traffic accident.
It is proved on record, by sufficient evidence as per law that the deceased succumbed to his injuries sustained in the road accident in question.

14. Further, copy of mechanical inspection report dated 09.09.2021 (which is also part of DAR) of Canter No. DL1GC-8286, would show fresh damages i.e. its front side bumper and both sides headlight were damaged; its front side body right side portion was damaged; its right side door window MACP No. 406/21; FIR No. 428/21; PS. Alipur DOD: 16.02.2024 was damaged and its front side windscreen middle portion glass was broken.

Likewise, copy of mechanical inspection report dated 09.06.2021 (which is also part of DAR) of Car bearing no. DL8C-AH-3688 of victim, would show that its front side body and bumper bonnet and both side headlight were damaged; its radiator and A/C condenser was damaged; its front side body frame was damaged; its battery and electric wiring was damaged; its front side windscreen glass was broken; its dashboard was damaged; its steering wheel and bracket were damaged; its clutch/brake padel bracket were bended; its front right side wheel rim was damaged and side wheel suspension was damaged.
There documents have not been disputed by the respondents and corroborate the ocular testimony of PW1 Sh. Naresh Kumar to the aforesaid extent.
Both these reports would also corroborate the testimony of PW1 to the effect that offending vehicle came from front side and hit the car of deceased from front side.
15. The site plan annexed with the criminal case record has been prepared during the investigation.
Perusal of the same clearly reveals that offending vehicle came from front side after changing its lane.

The spot of accident at point A as per site plan shows that deceased was driving his car at the correct side of the road, however, the respondent no. 1 had come from the front side at the road where the car of deceased was moving, after changing its lane and hit the car from the front side.

It is apparent that it was head on collision and despite best efforts of deceased to save the collision of his car MACP No. 406/21; FIR No. 428/21; PS. Alipur DOD: 16.02.2024 with the offending vehicle

,
he could not avert the collision and got collided with the offending vehicle from the front side.
The rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle may be proved, either by direct evidence or by circumstances including principle by applying the res-ipsa loquitur.

The nature and manner of damage to the car of deceased and the offending tempo due to collision clearly points out to rash and negligent manner of driving of offending vehicle by respondent no. 1/driver, thereby causing injuries to the deceased.
Moreover, the offending vehicle is shown to have been seized from the place of accident.

This fact gets strengthened from the copy of seizure memo dated 08/09.06.2021 (date of accident also being 08.06.2021) (which is part of DAR).
16.

In view of the aforesaid discussion and the evidence which has come on record, it is held that the petitioners have been able to prove on the basis of preponderance of probabilities that deceased has sustained fatal injuries in the Motor Vehicular Accident which has occurred on 08.06.2021, near Meadows Park, Delhi, due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle(Canter) bearing Naresh And Ors (Lrs Of Sachin Kumar) vs Saddam on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71861341/
5 registration no. DL1GC-8286 by respondent no. 1.
Thus, issue no. 1 is decided in favour of petitioners and against the respondents.

17. The petitioners who are claimants are the parents of deceased where petitioner no. 1 namely Sh.
Naresh Kumar is the father of deceased MACP No. 406/21; FIR No. 428/21; PS. Alipur DOD:
16.02.2024 and petitioner no. 2 Smt. Madhu is the mother of deceased.

In the present case, the road accident in question has led to fatal injuries to the victim namely Sachin Kumar, who could not be saved even though, he was immediately taken to the nearby hospital i.e. Kapil Hospital, Main Road Nathupura, Delhi.
It is an undisputed material on record that deceased was unmarried at the time of accident.
Further, the postmortem report (which is part of DAR) also corroborates that cause of death of deceased was hemorrhagic shock as a result of abdominal injuries due to blunt force impact.
Accordingly, petitioners are entitled for just and fair compensation in the present case.

18. Section 168 of the Motor Vehicle Act 1988 enjoins upon the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.

The guiding principles for assessment of "just and reasonable compensation" in fatal case has been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in case titled as Smt. Anjali & Ors.,
Vs.

Lokendra Rathod & Ors, in Civil Appeal No. 9014 of 202, decided on 06.12.2022 that: -
"The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short, "MV Act") gives paramount importance to the concept of 'just and fair' compensation.
It is a beneficial legislation which has been framed with the object of providing relief to the victims or their families.

Section 168 of the MV Act deals with the concept of 'just compensation'
which ought to be determined on the foundation of fairness, reasonableness and equitability.

Although such determination can never be arithmetically exact or perfect, an endeavor should be made MACP No. 406/21; FIR No. 428/21; PS. Alipur DOD: 16.02.2024 by the Court to award just and fair compensation irrespective of the amount claimed by the applicant/s.

In Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr.3, this Court has laid down as under:
"16.

sentences.text: "Just compensation" is adequate compensation which is fair and equitable, on the facts and circumstances of the case, to make good the loss suffered as a result of the wrong, as far as money can do so, by applying the well settled principles relating to award of compensation.
It is not intended to be a bonanza, largesse or source of profit."
19. The Hon'ble Apex Court has held that the compensation should be just and is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be niggardly or a pittance.
Reliance is placed on 2012 (8) SLT 676 titled K. Suresh Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd.

22 . During the course of arguments, Ld. counsel for petitioners fairly conceded that for want of any cogent and definite evidence being led by petitioners regarding monthly income of deceased, his income may be considered as per Minimum Wages Act in order to calculate the loss of MACP No.
406/21; FIR No. 428/21; PS. Alipur DOD: 16.02.2024 dependency.
It is contended that the deceased was working for gain at Delhi at the relevant time.
He has further prayed that future prospects be also awarded to the petitioners as he had promising future.
23. As already noted above, PW1 Sh. Naresh Kumar, who is father of deceased deposed in his evidence that deceased was earning Rs. 30,000/- per month at the time of accident.
However, he has not filed any documentary evidence in this regard.
Petitioners have filed copy of matriculation marksheet (Ex. PW1/5) in proof of educational qualification of deceased.
Hence, it is held that the petitioners have failed to prove that deceased was employed or earning any amount at the time of accident.

It may be noted here that petitioners have relied upon copy of voter I card of deceased,
wherein his address is of Delhi.
Thus, it is considered that deceased was permanent resident of Delhi.

However, for want of cogent and definite evidence being led by petitioners with regard to actual monthly income of deceased, his notional monthly income is being taken as equivalent to that of a matriculate person under Minimum Wages Act applicable during the relevant period.
The minimum wages of a matriculate person were Rs. 19,291/- per month as on the date of accident which is 08.06.2021.
